note: The machine-checkable subset of SPEC.md section 11. Section 11 is the human
record, with the reasoning and the evidence; this is the part a script can
confirm still holds against upstream. Editing section 11 means editing this
too - two allowlists drifting apart is the failure this file exists to catch,
one level up.
Entries check what the plugin actually reads, which is often a private
attribute rather than the public method beside it: `agent._access_points`,
not `get_access_points()`. Checking the public half would pass clean through
exactly the rename this is meant to catch.
It checks that symbols exist with the shape claimed. It cannot check that
they behave as claimed - that pwnagotchi.restart really touches those files,
that agent.session() really blocks - which is what the on-device run is for.
Not covered, deliberately: F12 lives in another repository
(abonforti/pwnagotchi-plugins) and is a soft dependency; F22 is a historical
note about the project this forks and describes bugs, not a dependency.
F29 is not covered either, for both reasons at once: its evidence is in that
same other repository (abonforti/pwnagotchi-plugins, pisugarx_ext.py), and the
upstream file of the identical shape, plugins/default/pisugarx.py, exists only
on the noai branch - on master it 404s, so there is nothing at the pinned tag
for a check to read.
Every other fact in section 11 has at least one entry here.
F28 is the reason an entry can now assert an absence. What agent.view() hands
back on a unit is a pwnagotchi.ui.display.Display, not a bare View, so the
delegation chain F28b and F28c pin holds only while Display declares no get of
its own - an override would intercept every read before View.get was reached.
F28d asserts that absence.
It needed a fourth entry, and the id convention used to stop at c:
tests/tools/test_pinned_facts mapped an entry back to its section 11 fact with
id.rstrip('abc'). That capped a fact at three files for no reason anyone chose,
and would have left this half of F28 checked by review rather than by anything
that runs. It now matches the F-number instead, so a fact may have as many
entries as it has files to rest on.

face_status calls agent.view(); a rename leaves the plugin reporting an empty face for ever

the reader the plugin calls, its body, and the two keys it asks for. The body is pinned and not just the signature: _view_text has no widget-unwrapping branch, so a View.get that stopped delegating to State.get and handed back the element would keep this signature, keep both keys, and turn every face into an empty string on a healthy unit. If either key leaves the initial state, get answers None and face_status goes silently blank

text: return self._state[key].value if key in self._state else None
facts.why: the return contract, not just the name: the value rather than the widget, and None for an absent key. _view_text has no widget-unwrapping branch because this line says it cannot happen

agent.view() returns a Display, not a bare View, so the delegation chain F28b and F28c pin only holds while Display adds no get of its own. An override here would intercept every read before View.get is reached, and the plugin would never know
the one place the ready event is emitted. A plugin gets its agent from this line or from nowhere, which is what makes manual mode agent-less (issue #140)

neither entry point emits ready itself, so the only route to it is agent.start(), which do_auto_mode calls and do_manual_mode does not. Pinned as an absence because the absence is what makes the manual path agent-less; the day cli.py emits ready, this plugin can start its threads from on_ready again

the second route to the ready event, off the boot path: toggle_plugin fires it at the single plugin it enables and hands over view.ROOT._agent, so a plugin switched on from the web UI receives an agent in any mode. Pinned because F31's rule is about how a unit boots rather than about the event, and a reader who finds this call without the row would reasonably conclude the row is wrong

the three calls that make up load_from_file. It checks that all three are still present in the file, which is what it can check: contains_all is not scoped to one function and cannot see a fourth call added beside them. The half that carries the fact is F30b

the loader never registers the plugin module, so during import sys.modules.get(__name__) is None and any module-scope construct that resolves its own module by name dies. That made the plugin unloadable on every unit (issue #136) while the suite stayed green, because pytest imports it the ordinary way. Pinned as an absence because the absence is the fact: the day upstream adds a registration this constraint lifts, and we should hear about it rather than keep working around something that no longer applies
